notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found for the open-mode tier after a failed OPEN). Not implemented: one path of item b. §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR11 b runs "any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1", and §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR5 b associates a USE ... ON INPUT procedure with "any file open in the input mode or in the process of being opened in the input mode". FileConnector.OpenOnceEntered records the mode of an OPEN that fails and nothing clears it until a successful CLOSE, so FileConnector.OpenModeView still answers that mode to the open-mode tier (EmitScopeTiers) for every later statement: a READ of a file that is not open, executed after a failed OPEN INPUT, runs the USE ... ON INPUT procedure, where the same READ before any OPEN (and after a CLOSE) runs none. The mechanism is the USE statement's (§1985:VII.4.6.4 GR5 b to e), reaches every I-O statement of the three file modules at every edition (probed the same at --std 2023), and is recorded once more on 1985-GR-VII.4.7.4-10 of this slice. Implemented at 85, everything else: SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRead renders the rule's branches on the outcome of the runtime read: in the success branch EmitRecordAreaStore fills the record area, the FILE STATUS item is stored, the bound INTO move (MoveBinder.BindIntoPhrase) runs and then the NOT AT END statements (EmitNotPhrase); in the failure branch the status is stored, EmitUseHook runs, and the AT END statements are guarded by IoStatusClass.AtEnd, so a 4x or 3x status skips them ("the AT END phrase is ignored, if specified"). The hook's __IoCheck (EmitUseMachinery) runs the file-name USE procedure, else the open-mode one, and returns to the statement after the READ. SequentialConnector.ReadRecord advances the position to the record made available and ends in FileConnector.ReadSucceeded (item a). The 2023 proviso the change record turns on (the indicator is not set on a record operation conflict) is unreachable in a 1985 run unit, since FileRegistry.RecordLocksSetUnder sets locks only under a LOCK MODE clause and that clause, SHARING and the READ lock phrases are refused at 85 (COBOL0900, probed). Probed at --std 85: a READ of a file open for output and of a closed file (47), each with both phrases, runs the file-name USE procedure (the USE ... ON OUTPUT one for an open output file no USE names) and neither phrase; a READ answering 46 with an AT END phrase runs the USE procedure and not the phrase; a successful READ INTO a subscripted item evaluates the subscript before NOT AT END changes it and runs NOT AT END after the move. The witness runs item c with INTO and an AT END phrase that is ignored.

next.reason: CHANGED on item a alone (round-1 ruling, difference 2), the ground of its siblings VIII.4.5.4 GR11 and IX.4.5.4 GR11, whose item a has the same words. 1985: 'The file position indicator is set and the I-O status associated with file-name-1 is updated' (§1985:VII.4.4.4 GR11) for every READ the rule covers, and after an unsuccessful one 'the file position indicator is set to indicate that no valid next record has been established' (§1985:VII.4.4.4 GR12). 2023: 'The I-O status associated with file-name-1 is updated and, if the record operation conflict condition did not occur, the file position indicator is set' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR13), and for that condition 'The file position indicator is unchanged' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR10). The words that differ are 'if the record operation conflict condition did not occur': a case removed from the 1985 result. A program with no post-1985 syntax reaches the condition: with no SHARING phrase or clause 'the implementor shall define the sharing mode that is established for each file connector' (§2023:14.9.27.4 GR23); with no LOCK MODE clause 'the type of record locking for that opening of a shared file associated with that file connector is defined by the implementor' (§2023:12.4.5.9.4 GR1); and when 'the record identified for access is locked by another file connector', 'the record operation conflict condition exists' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR9). Record locking is not confined to relative and indexed files: the LOCK MODE clause excludes for a sequential file only its MULTIPLE phrase ('The MULTIPLE phrase shall not be specified for a file described with sequential organization or sequential access mode', §2023:12.4.5.9.3 SR2). The earlier KEPT rested on 'The conflict proviso reaches only record locking', which 1985 'cannot write': the premise round 1 refuted with those rules. The opening and items b and c are carried and are no ground. Opening: 1985 'If an at end condition does not occur during the execution of a READ statement, the AT END phrase is ignored, if specified'; 2023 'If neither an at end nor an invalid key condition occurs during the execution of a READ statement, the AT END phrase or the INVALID KEY phrase is ignored, if specified' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR13). The 1985 sequential READ has no INVALID KEY phrase and its rule names none, which is the reason its own text gives for listing no rule of 9.1.14 where the relative and indexed GR11 list three. b: 1985 'control is transferred according to rules of the USE statement following the execution of any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1'; 2023 'control is transferred according to the rules in 9.1.12, Input-output exception processing. If the exception condition is not a fatal exception condition, control is then transferred to the end of the READ statement' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR13), 9.1.12 naming the USE declarative ('Statements in a file-exception or exception-name format of a USE declarative', §2023:9.1.12 GR2), which runs 'upon the unsuccessful execution of an input-output operation unless an AT END or INVALID KEY phrase takes precedence' (§2023:14.9.49.4 GR6) and after which 'control is returned to an implicit CONTINUE statement following the input-output statement whose execution caused the exception' (§2023:14.9.49.4 GR7). The fatal wording is no change: 1985 already says 'If the I-O status value does indicate a critical error, the implementor determines what action is taken' and otherwise 'returns control to the next executable statement following the input-output statement whose execution caused the exception' (§1985:VII.4.6.4 GR6). c: the record is made available, the INTO move is executed, and 1985's 'Control is transferred to the end of the READ statement or to imperative-statement-2, if specified' is 2023's 'if the NOT AT END phrase or NOT INVALID KEY phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR13). The WHEN phrase of 9.1.12 needs an exception-checking PERFORM 1985 cannot write and this rule refuses nothing, so under the family ruling it is no ground. Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993) reworded b only.
